subject: Immunology
topic: Acute Interstitial Nephritis Drug Hypersensitivity and Eosinophiluria
stem: A 58-year-old man who was started on oral omeprazole for gastroesophageal reflux disease and amoxicillin-clavulanate for acute sinusitis 12 days ago presents with a low-grade fever, a generalized maculopapular erythematous skin rash on his trunk, and dull bilateral flank ache. Physical examination reveals an oral temperature of 38.3 C and mild bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness. Laboratory evaluation demonstrates: - Serum Creatinine: 2.8 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL 1 month ago) - Complete Blood Count: WBC 11,800/mcL with 14% eosinophils (marked peripheral eosinophilia; absolute eosinophil count 1,650/mcL) Urinalysis reveals 1+ protein, 2+ blood, and marked sterile pyuria (20-30 WBCs/hpf; urine culture is completely negative). Hansel staining of the urinary sediment reveals that > 10% of excreted leukocytes are EOSINOPHILS. Centrifuged urine examination confirms the presence of WHITE BLOOD CELL CASTS. Renal biopsy demonstrates intense interstitial edema and a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed of T lymphocytes, macrophages, and abundant eosinophils, with sparing of glomeruli. Which of the following pathophysiological mechanisms is responsible for this patient's acute renal dysfunction?

options.text: Direct chemical necrosis of the proximal tubular brush border mediated by accumulated nephrotoxic drug crystals
options.explanation: Crystal-induced nephropathy is caused by acyclovir, indinavir, sulfadiazine, or methotrexate, which precipitate in tubules causing mechanical obstruction without eosinophilia or rash.

options.text: Circulating immune complex deposition in the mesangium triggering alternative complement pathway activation
options.explanation: Immune complex deposition in mesangium causes glomerulonephritis (IgA nephropathy, lupus), characterized by red blood cell casts, not white blood cell casts or eosinophiluria.

options.text: Autoantibody-mediated binding to the non-collagenous domain of Type IV collagen in glomerular capillaries
options.explanation: This is Anti-GBM disease, which produces crescentic GN and linear IgG on immunofluorescence, not interstitial eosinophilic nephritis.

options.text: Drug-induced type IV (cell-mediated) and type I hypersensitivity reaction directed against renal tubular basement membrane hapten antigens
options.explanation: Correct. Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN; tubulointerstitial nephritis) is an immunologically mediated adverse drug reaction accounting for ~15% of unexplained acute kidney injury in hospitalized adults. The most common causative pharmacologic culprits are: (1) PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS (omeprazole, pantoprazole); (2) ANTIBIOTICS (penicillins, cephalosporins, sulfonamides, rifampin); and (3) NSAIDS. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The offending drug (or its metabolite) acts as a HAPTEN, covalently binding to components of the tubular basement membrane or cytoplasmic proteins. This hapten-protein conjugate is processed by dendritic cells and presented to T cells, triggering a combined TYPE IV (DELAYED-TYPE, T-CELL MEDIATED) AND TYPE I (IGA/IGE-MEDIATED) HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTION. Activated T lymphocytes and mast cells release cytokines (IL-5), recruiting EOSINOPHILS into the renal interstitium. Classic clinical triad (seen in ~10-15%): FEVER, MACULOPAPULAR RASH, and PERIPHERAL EOSINOPHILIA, occurring 1 to 3 weeks post-exposure. URINALYSIS HALLMARKS: Sterile pyuria, EOSINOPHILURIA (demonstrated by Hansel or Wright stain), and WHITE BLOOD CELL CASTS (which confirm tubular/interstitial inflammation, distinguishing it from lower urinary tract cystitis). Treatment requires immediate cessation of the offending drug +/- corticosteroids.

options.text: Non-enzymatic glycation of efferent arterioles leading to glomerular hyperfiltration and sclerosis
options.explanation: Non-enzymatic glycation causes diabetic nephropathy, not acute drug hypersensitivity with fever, rash, and eosinophils.

subject: Pathology
topic: Renal Cell Carcinoma VHL Gene Deletion and HIF-1-Alpha
stem: A 59-year-old man presents with painless gross hematuria, a dull ache in his left flank, and a 12-lb unintended weight loss over the past 3 months. Physical examination reveals a palpable, firm, non-tender mass in the left upper quadrant of his abdomen and a non-reducing left-sided scrotal varicocele that fails to decompress when lying recumbent. Laboratory evaluation reveals: - Hemoglobin: 19.4 g/dL (marked secondary polycythemia; hematocrit 58%) - Serum Calcium: 11.8 mg/dL (hypercalcemia) - Erythropoietin (EPO): Markedly elevated Abdominal contrast-enhanced CT reveals a 7.5-cm, highly vascular, solid, heterogeneous mass arising from the upper pole of the left kidney, with a tumor thrombus extending into the left renal vein. Radical nephrectomy is performed. Histopathological examination demonstrates sheets and nests of rounded polygonal epithelial cells with abundant clear cytoplasm, separated by a delicate, arborizing network of thin-walled sinusoidal blood vessels. Cytogenetic analysis reveals a loss-of-function mutation and loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 3p. The constitutive upregulation of which of the following transcription factors directly drives the marked vascularity and paraneoplastic polycythemia in this neoplasm?

options.text: c-Myc oncogene driving uncontrolled transcription of ribosome biogenesis proteins and metabolic reprogramming
options.explanation: c-Myc is amplified in Burkitt lymphoma t(8;14) and small cell carcinomas, not the primary chromosome 3p VHL pathway of clear cell RCC.

options.text: Retinoblastoma protein (Rb) driving uninhibited progression from G2 phase to M phase of the cell cycle
options.explanation: Rb regulates the G1/S transition (not G2/M), and is mutated in retinoblastoma and osteosarcoma, not clear cell RCC.

options.text: Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappa-B) promoting anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 expression in lymphoid germinal centers
options.explanation: NF-kB drives inflammatory and lymphoid signaling (e.g., Reed-Sternberg cells in Hodgkin lymphoma), not VHL/HIF clear cell angiogenesis.

options.text: Forkhead box protein P3 (FOXP3) directing the differentiation of immunosuppressive regulatory T cells
options.explanation: FOXP3 is the master transcription factor for Treg lymphocytes (mutated in IPEX syndrome), completely unrelated to renal cell carcinoma.

options.text: Hypoxia-inducible factor-1-alpha (HIF-1-alpha), driving excessive transcription of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and erythropoietin (EPO)
options.explanation: Correct. Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common primary renal malignancy (> 75-80% of RCC). Origin: PROXIMAL CONVOLUTED TUBULE epithelial cells. Histology: Polygonal cells with abundant CLEAR CYTOPLASM (filled with accumulated glycogen and lipids that dissolve during routine histological processing), surrounded by dense arborizing capillary networks. MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS: In > 90% of sporadic clear cell RCC and in hereditary von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease, there is a loss-of-function mutation or deletion on CHROMOSOME 3P25 (VHL GENE). Normally, the VHL protein functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase component: in the presence of oxygen, prolyl hydroxylases hydroxylate HYPOXIA-INDUCIBLE FACTOR-1-ALPHA (HIF-1-alpha), allowing VHL to bind HIF-1-alpha and target it for ubiquitin-proteasome degradation. Loss of VHL prevents HIF-1-alpha degradation. HIF-1-ALPHA ACCUMULATES CONSTITUTIVELY, translocating to the nucleus where it drives uninhibited transcription of hypoxia-responsive genes: (1) VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR (VEGF) and PDGF -> massive neo-angiogenesis and hypervascularity; (2) ERYTHROPOIETIN (EPO) -> paraneoplastic secondary POLYCYTHEMIA; (3) Parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) -> paraneoplastic HYPERCALCEMIA. (Left-sided varicocele occurs because the left gonadal vein drains into the left renal vein, which is obstructed by tumor thrombus).
